--- title: "Final Project: Energy Consumption Forecasting" subtitle: "MATH840: Time Series" author: "Ihor Miroshnychenko" institute: Kyiv School of Economics format: html: highlight-style: github theme: [default, custom.scss] execute: echo: true warning: false editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- # Introduction & Scenario You are acting as a Data Scientist for a regional energy distributor. The company needs to plan reserve power generation for the next **48 hours** to ensure grid stability and minimize costs. Your task is to predict electricity consumption (in kWh) based on historical data. However, point predictions are not enough—grid operators need to know the **uncertainty** of your forecast to manage risks. Therefore, you must provide both a forecast and a **95% Prediction Interval**. # Data Description You are provided with a training dataset [`train.csv`](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/182acVDJGWXB9y4831VId4NEizo6RI7hg36y-rt7cYlc/edit?usp=sharing) containing historical energy consumption recorded every **15 minutes**. ### Dataset Structure | Column | Description | Format | |--------|-------------|--------| | `Date` | Date of observation | `MM/DD/YYYY` | | `Time` | Time of observation | `HH:MM:SS` | | `Value` | Energy consumption (kWh) | Float | **Data Preview:** ```csv Date,Time,Value 8/28/2025,22:00:00,33.33 8/28/2025,22:15:00,44.44 8/28/2025,22:30:00,55.55 ... ``` # Part 1: In-Class Prediction (Tuesday) **Objective:** Build a model and generate a forecast for the "Hidden Test Set". ## Technical Requirements 1. **Forecast Horizon:** The next **48 hours** immediately following the last timestamp in your training data (Total: **192 steps**). 2. **Output:** * **Point Forecast:** The expected value. * **Prediction Interval (95%):** Lower and Upper bounds. ## Submission Format You must upload a CSV file named `SURNAME_submission.csv` containing exactly **192 rows** with the following columns: * `Date` * `Time` * `Forecast` (Predicted Value) * `Lower_95` (Lower Bound of 95% CI) * `Upper_95` (Upper Bound of 95% CI) ## Evaluation Metrics Your submission will be evaluated automatically against the ground truth using three metrics. ### 1. Accuracy: RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error) Penalizes large errors significantly. $$ RMSE = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{t=1}^{n}(y_t - \hat{y}_t)^2} $$ ### 2. Interpretability: MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error) Shows the error relative to the actual value. $$ MAPE = \frac{100\%}{n}\sum_{t=1}^{n}\left| \frac{y_t - \hat{y}_t}{y_t} \right| $$ ### 3. Uncertainty: Winkler Score Evaluates the quality of your prediction intervals. It rewards narrow intervals but penalizes heavily if the true value falls outside the interval. For a $(1-\alpha)$ interval (where $\alpha=0.05$): $$ S_t = \begin{cases} U_t - L_t & \text{if } L_t \le y_t \le U_t \\ (U_t - L_t) + \frac{2}{\alpha}(L_t - y_t) & \text{if } y_t < L_t \\ (U_t - L_t) + \frac{2}{\alpha}(y_t - U_t) & \text{if } y_t > U_t \end{cases} $$ $$ \text{Winkler Score} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{t=1}^{n} S_t $$ * **Goal:** Minimize all three metrics. * **Ranking:** The final rank will be a weighted average of rankings in these three categories. ### 4. FINAL SCORE The final score will be computed as follows: $$ R_{final} = 0.3 \cdot Rank_{RMSE} + 0.3 \cdot Rank_{MAPE} + 0.4 \cdot Rank_{Winkler} $$ # Part 2: Final Report (Friday) After the initial submission, you have time until Friday to improve your model and prepare a report. **Deliverables:** 1. **Updated Forecast:** (Optional) If you improved your model, submit a new CSV. 2. **Report / Presentation:** A Jupyter Notebook or PDF covering: * **EDA:** What patterns (seasonality, trend) did you find? * **Methodology:** Why did you choose this model? * **Diagnostics:** Residual analysis. * **Evaluation:** Local cross-validation results. * **Improvement:** How did you handle the prediction intervals? # Rules & Tips 1. **Tools:** You may use any programming language (Python, R) and any library. 2. **External Data:** Use of external datasets (weather, holidays) is allowed but must be documented. 3. **Negative Values:** Energy consumption cannot be negative. Ensure your Lower Bound $\ge 0$. --- # Assessment and Grading The final project contributes **32 points** to the total course grade. The grade is based on individual performance and consists of two main components: quantitative forecast accuracy (Model Performance) and qualitative analysis (Analytical Quality). 1. **Model Performance (20 points):** This score is determined by the accuracy of the forecast on a hidden test set. Grading follows a **benchmark-based approach**: * **Baseline Threshold (15 points):** Awarded to any student whose model outperforms a standard baseline (e.g., Seasonal Naive method). This ensures that a scientifically sound model receives a high grade regardless of peer performance. * **Competitive Bonus (up to 5 points):** Additional points are awarded to the top-performing models that demonstrate significant accuracy improvements over the baseline. 2. **Analytical Quality (12 points):** This component evaluates the depth of the research, the correctness of the methodology, code reproducibility, and the clarity of the final report. The final deliverables include: 1. Submission CSV file (generated during the in-class session). 2. A written report (Jupyter Notebook or PDF). 3. Reproducible code (submitted via GitHub or archive). 4. Presentation slides (summary of findings). **Criteria and Point Breakdown (Total: 32 points):** | Criteria | Points | Description | | :--- | :---: | :--- | | **Forecast Accuracy** | **20** | **Base (15 pts):** Beating the baseline benchmark (proving the model captures signal better than a naive approach).
**Bonus (5 pts):** Top-tier accuracy ranking relative to the class distribution (RMSE/MAPE/Winkler). | | **Methodology & Diagnostics** | **5** | Justification of model selection, correctness of cross-validation setup, residual analysis (ACF/PACF), and proper handling of seasonality. | | **EDA & Visualization** | **3** | Quality of data exploration, identification of key patterns (trends, cycles, anomalies), and clarity of graphical representation. | | **Code Quality** | **2** | Code structure, reproducibility (must run without errors), and readability (comments/documentation). | | **Report & Presentation** | **2** | Structure of the narrative, clarity of conclusions, and quality of presentation materials. | --- ### Appendix: Submission Template Generation (Python) You can use this snippet to generate your submission file structure: ::: {#4f7ed75b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd future_index = pd.date_range( start='2025-08-27 00:00:00', periods=192, freq='15min' ) submission = pd.DataFrame({ 'Date': future_index.date, 'Time': future_index.time, 'Forecast': 0.0, # Replace with your predictions 'Lower_95': 0.0, # Replace with your lower bound 'Upper_95': 0.0 # Replace with your upper bound }) submission.to_csv('SURNAME_submission.csv', index=False) ``` :::
